t: First Letter Capitalization — SQL String Transformation
o: Transform each content_text to title case: first letter of each word uppercase, the rest lowercase, spaces preserved. 'hello world of SQL' becomes 'Hello World Of Sql'; 'TOP rated programming BOOKS' becomes 'Top Rated Programming Books'. Since there are no special characters, words are simply space-delimited tokens. In SQL we split each row into its words, title-case each token, and re-concatenate in order.
k: Split on spaces, apply UPPER(first char) + LOWER(rest) per token, then rejoin preserving single-space structure.

a.i: A numbers table drives word extraction: SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(text, ' ', n), ' ', -1) yields the nth word. Title-case each word with CONCAT(UPPER(LEFT(w,1)), LOWER(SUBSTRING(w,2))), limit n to the word count (spaces + 1), and rebuild the sentence with GROUP_CONCAT ... SEPARATOR ' '.
s: Extract the nth word of each row via nested SUBSTRING_INDEX.
Title-case each word and GROUP_CONCAT in numeric order with a space separator, restricted to n <= word count.

c.python:
SELECT content_id,
       content_text AS original_text,
       (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(
                 CONCAT(UPPER(SUBSTRING(w, 1, 1)), LOWER(SUBSTRING(w, 2)))
                 ORDER BY n SEPARATOR ' ')
        FROM (
          SELECT nums.n,
                 SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(u.content_text, ' ', nums.n), ' ', -1) AS w
          FROM (SELECT 1 n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
                UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8
                UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12
                UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16
                UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20) nums
        ) t
        WHERE n <= 1 + LENGTH(content_text) - LENGTH(REPLACE(content_text, ' ', ''))) AS converted_text
FROM user_content u;

a.t: O(rows * words * length) — each word extraction scans the string a constant number of times.
a.sp: O(words) temporary per row for grouping.

w: The word-count guard (LENGTH minus REPLACE trick) ensures trailing numbers do not inject empty tokens. Pitfalls: forgetting ORDER BY inside GROUP_CONCAT (word order not guaranteed otherwise), assuming a fixed word count (extend the numbers table if needed), and double spaces (the problem guarantees normal spacing; otherwise a recursive splitter would be needed). Follow-up: preserve mixed-case acronyms, or handle punctuation-adjacent words.
